patients.summary: Chicopee demolition laborer with COPD, hypertension and a long pack-a-day habit who joins in 2018, has occupational lead poisoning in 2022, then stage IIIB right upper lobe NSCLC in late 2023 treated with chemoradiation, durvalumab and later SBRT to a right lower lobe site; quits smoking April 2024; pulmonary aspergilloma found November 2025.

documents.title: New patient - records
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Hi. I signed up for the membership last week. My doctor in Springfield retired in the spring and I have been running low on my inhalers. I use the purple disk one twice a day, the rescue inhaler, and a water pill for blood pressure. What do you need from me to get my old records over? First appointment is the 21st.
Todd Rossi

documents.title: RE: New patient - records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Todd, welcome to the practice. I attached a records release form; sign it and send it back here or bring it on the 21st. Once we have it we will request your chart from the Springfield office. Please bring all your inhalers and pill bottles to the first visit. If you run out of anything before then, message us and the doctor can send a bridge refill.

Last BP in their records was at goal on HCTZ.
No spirometry, chest CT or sleep study in packet.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

51M demolition laborer transferring care; prior PCP in Springfield retired. Records reviewed (abstract in chart).

HPI: Here to establish. Carries a diagnosis of COPD made clinically by his old doctor years ago; as far as he knows he never had breathing tests, and none are in the records. Uses fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 one inhalation twice a day, fairly consistent, and albuterol a few times a week, more with exertion at work. Gets short of breath carrying loads up stairs on jobs, says it has been like that for a while. Morning cough most days, which he attributes to smoking. No recent flares, no ED visits, no oral steroids this year that he recalls. Hypertension on HCTZ 25 for years, no side effects, does not check at home.

Tobacco: 1 ppd since age 13, about 38 pack-years. Never seriously tried to quit.
Alcohol: 1-2 drinks a month. No drugs.
Work: demolition crew for a commercial contractor, a lot of dust; admits he usually skips the mask.
Lives in Chicopee.

PMH: COPD, HTN, tobacco use.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 12.
Meds: as above, reconciled.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father lung cancer dx at 68, deceased. Mother COPD. Brother HTN.
Screening: colonoscopy 2017 normal, due 2027.

ROS: chronic morning cough, exertional dyspnea as above. Denies chest pain, hemoptysis, weight change, fevers, leg swelling.

Exam: BP 132/80, HR 75, SpO2 94% RA, T 36.6, Wt 80.0 kg, Ht 178.6 cm, BMI 25.1.
Well appearing, talkative. Smells of smoke. Neck supple, no LAD. Lungs: clear, no wheeze or crackles. CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Abd soft, nontender. Ext: no edema, no cyanosis.

A/P
1. COPD, clinical diagnosis, never confirmed by spirometry. Symptoms stable on ICS/LABA + PRN SABA. Continue fluticasone-salmeterol and albuterol, refills sent. Will look at getting formal PFTs at some point.
2. HTN, at goal on HCTZ 25. BMP today.
3. Tobacco use disorder, 1 ppd. Talked through the link with his lungs and his father's cancer. He listened but is not ready to set a quit date. Offered patch or varenicline whenever he wants them.
4. Health maintenance: Tdap today (last Td 2007). Lipids, BMP, one-time HCV and HIV screening today. Flu shot when available in the fall. PHQ-2 negative.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed. Gave him the practice cell number for texts.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Todd, your labs from Tuesday are back. Kidney function (creatinine 1.03) and potassium (4.2) look fine on the HCTZ. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are both negative, so those are done. Your cholesterol panel is attached (LDL 145, HDL 31); we will go over it at the next visit. Text me with any questions.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after work for flu vaccine. Screening questions negative, no egg or vaccine reactions in the past, not ill today. Quadrivalent influenza 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, lot recorded. Tolerated well, waited 15 min, left without issue.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6-month check. Winter so far uneventful by his account. Breathing at baseline; albuterol a few times a week. Taking HCTZ daily. Still 1 ppd. Busy at work, a hospital wing teardown.

O: BP 133/85, HR 82, SpO2 96%, Wt 79.4 kg.
Lungs clear, good air movement. CV RRR. No edema.

A/P:
- HTN: fine on HCTZ 25, continue.
- COPD: stable, continue ICS/LABA and PRN albuterol. Inhaler technique checked, good.
- Tobacco: discussed again, gave quitline card. Not ready to pick a date. Will keep asking.
RTC August for physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

52M. No new concerns. Breathing about the same as last year: winded on stairs with a load, fine on flat ground. Morning cough. No flares since he joined. HCTZ daily.
Tobacco 1 ppd, roughly 39 pack-years. Alcohol rare. Still on the demolition crew.

ROS otherwise negative: no chest pain, no hemoptysis, no weight loss, no GI or GU complaints. Mood good.
PHQ-2: 0.

Meds: fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN, HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA.
FHx unchanged (father lung ca, mother COPD, brother HTN).

Exam: BP 130/79, HR 84, SpO2 95%, Wt 78.9 kg, BMI 24.9.
Gen NAD. HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx clear, tonsils surgically absent. Neck no thyromegaly or nodes. Lungs: clear bilaterally, no wheeze or crackles. CV: RRR, normal S1 S2. Abd: soft, NT, no masses. Skin: no concerning lesions. Ext: no edema. Neuro grossly nonfocal.

Assessment/plan:
- Preventive: BMP and lipid panel drawn. Shingrix dose 1 today, dose 2 in 2-6 months. Colonoscopy up to date (2017). Tdap 2018.
- COPD stable on current inhalers.
- HTN at goal.
- Tobacco: brief counseling. Declines quit date, declines meds for now.
Follow up 6 months.

documents.title: Flu shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Walk-in before work for seasonal flu vaccine. Afebrile, no complaints. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. No reaction. Reminded him Shingrix #2 is due next month; scheduled 11/19.

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second recombinant zoster dose given IM L deltoid. After dose 1 in August he had a sore arm for two days and felt run down one evening, nothing else. Counseled that the second dose can do the same. Series complete.

documents.title: No-show follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt missed 1/27 follow-up. Reached him on cell, he was on a job site and forgot. Rebooked for 2/11 at 4 pm, after his shift.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from 1/27.
Doing OK. Breathing "same as always." Inhalers daily, albuterol most days now that it is cold out on site. HCTZ daily, no lightheadedness.
Smoking: still a pack a day. When asked about quitting: "Not this year."

Vitals: BP 134/79, HR 68, SpO2 94%, wt 80.0 kg.
Chest: clear to auscultation, no focal findings. Heart regular rate. Legs without swelling.

1. HTN - at goal, continue HCTZ.
2. COPD - unchanged. Continue current inhalers. Reviewed when to call (fever, change in sputum, worse breathing).
3. Tobacco use - counseled, ~3 min. Not ready. Patch/varenicline offer stands.
Back in summer for annual.

documents.title: Pneumonia treated at urgent care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt texted, then I called him back. Last Tuesday (4/14) he went to an urgent care near a job in Holyoke with fever and a worse cough; was told he had pneumonia on a chest x-ray and was given an antibiotic, which he finished yesterday. He did not keep the paperwork. Fever gone since the weekend, cough improving, back at his baseline breathing. Using albuterol a little more than usual.
He mentions this is not the first time this past year he has been treated at urgent care for a chest infection, but this was the first one called pneumonia.

Plan: no further antibiotics needed with this improvement. Return precautions reviewed (fever back, worse breathing, chest pain). Asked him to call us first next time so we can see him the same day. We will get a follow-up chest x-ray at his physical in July to make sure it cleared.

documents.title: Annual Physical Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

53M, no complaints today.
Interval: pneumonia in April treated at urgent care (see 4/21 phone note), fully recovered. On further questioning he has had several chest infections over the past year, all treated with antibiotics at urgent care clinics near his job sites rather than here; he could not give dates or names of drugs. No hospital stays.
Still on the demolition crew. Lots of dust on the current job and he is honest that he mostly does not wear a mask.
He asks about a research study he saw advertised that is looking for workers with dust exposure. I printed the study's information sheet and contact line for him; he will decide on his own whether to call.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily for BP; fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 BID; albuterol PRN. NKDA.
Tobacco: still 1 ppd, now about 40 pack-years.
PHQ-2 0.

Vitals: BP 138/86, HR 78, RR 16.
Gen: well, no distress. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. CV RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, nontender. Ext no edema, no clubbing. Skin and neuro unremarkable.

CXR today (follow-up film after April pneumonia): no acute disease.
Labs drawn today, will release when back.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance - labs drawn (CBC, BMP fasting, lipids). Shingrix complete. Flu shot in the fall.
2. COPD - stable today, but repeated chest infections this past year and he has never had spirometry. Referring to pulmonology for evaluation and formal PFTs.
3. Pneumonia, April 2020 - resolved; follow-up film clear.
4. HTN - BP 138/86, upper end of goal, continue HCTZ, recheck next visit.
5. Tobacco use - counseled at length. He still declines a quit date. Quitline info again.
6. Occupational dust - encouraged a fitted respirator on dusty jobs.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Todd, your labs from Monday: blood count normal (hemoglobin 15, white count 7.0, platelets 250). Fasting sugar 96 and kidney function (creatinine 1.0) are normal. Cholesterol: total 220, LDL 150, HDL 30, triglycerides 200 - full report attached. Chest x-ray was clear. Pulmonology will call you to schedule; let me know if you have not heard from them in two weeks.

documents.title: Pulmonology referral status
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, has not heard from pulmonology. Called their office: referral received; they are booking new patients into November because of the COVID backlog. First available 11/16 at 10:30, pt accepted. Added to waitlist for earlier opening.

documents.title: Influenza immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Screened at door for COVID symptoms, negative. Flu vaccine quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. Observed, no reaction. Reminded of pulmonology appointment 11/16.

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry performed in the pulmonary function laboratory. Technique acceptable and reproducible. FEV1/FVC ratio is reduced, below the lower limit of normal, consistent with airflow obstruction. After inhaled albuterol there is some improvement, but the ratio remains below the lower limit of normal: the obstruction is only partially reversible.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory defect with incomplete reversibility after bronchodilator, consistent with COPD.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison 7/20/2020. The lungs are hyperinflated with flattening of both hemidiaphragms. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. No acute osseous abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms, consistent with COPD. No acute process.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 11/16/2020
Referred by: primary care, for COPD evaluation

Reason for referral: COPD carried as a clinical diagnosis without spirometry; recurrent chest infections.

History: Mr. Rossi is a 54-year-old demolition worker. His breathing has been getting worse; he now gets winded climbing one flight of stairs. He coughs every day and brings up yellowish phlegm, most of it first thing in the morning. No fever, chills or chest pain. Over the last year he has needed antibiotics for several chest infections, treated at urgent care. His primary care physician saw him in July for a physical and tobacco counseling.
He continues to smoke a pack a day and tells me he is not ready to stop. Works in construction around a lot of dust and wears a mask only now and then.

Medications: fluticasone propionate/salmeterol 250/50 one inhalation BID; albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h PRN; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: father with lung cancer (age 68), mother with COPD, brother with hypertension.

Examination: BP 131/81, pulse 66, SpO2 96% at rest on room air, weight 80.0 kg. Barrel-shaped chest. Breath sounds decreased throughout with scattered rhonchi. Nicotine staining of the fingernails. No digital clubbing. No cyanosis. Heart sounds regular. No leg edema.

Data:
- Sputum cultures: negative.
- Blood work today: unremarkable.
- Chest radiograph: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms.
- PFTs: airflow obstruction, only partly reversible after bronchodilator.
- Six-minute walk: limited by breathlessness, and his oxygen saturation fell during the walk.

Impression: COPD, now confirmed by spirometry, with a chronic bronchitis phenotype (daily productive cough) and frequent infectious exacerbations. Ongoing tobacco use and occupational dust exposure.

Recommendations:
1. Smoking cessation discussed at length; he declined a quit date.
2. Continue his current long-term inhaled regimen.
3. Referral placed to pulmonary rehabilitation.
4. Pulmonary follow-up in one year, sooner if needed.

Thank you for involving us in his care.
Pulmonology
